issues.description: Self-approval defeats the human approval gate. REQ-004 AC2b exempts every write under `<workspace_root>/docs/specs/` unconditionally, while REQ-002 AC2/AC3 and REQ-004 AC3 treat the `Status` cell of `docs/specs/INDEX.md` as the sole proof of human approval. An agent can therefore write `| ... | Approved |` into INDEX.md (or edit the package's own spec/design/tasks files) and immediately satisfy the gate with no human involvement, reproducing exactly the pre-approval mutation path described in Problem Statement item 2. The spec must define an approval artifact the gated agent cannot author (out-of-band approval record, non-agent-writable path, or runtime-held approval state) and state which actor may transition a spec into `EXECUTION_STATUSES`.

Contradiction on repositories without `docs/specs/`. REQ-002 AC2 states without qualification that code-mutating operations require at least one valid `EXECUTION_STATUSES` package, while REQ-004 AC3 scopes the same rule to 'a repository that has a `docs/specs/` directory', and design.md step 2 returns `valid: true` for `no_spec_framework`. An implementer following REQ-002 would deny every mutation in repositories that never adopted docs/specs (breaking the plugin everywhere); one following REQ-004 would allow them. The spec must state which applies and whether the gate is opt-in per workspace.

Authorization is global, not feature-scoped. REQ-002 AC2, REQ-004 AC3 and REQ-006 AC1 authorize a mutation when *any* `EXECUTION_STATUSES` package validates; there is no mapping from the target file to the authorizing feature, and `--feature` is optional (REQ-006 AC2). Consequently an approved spec for feature A permits arbitrary edits to feature B's code, and a stale approved spec keeps the gate open indefinitely. This contradicts REQ-006's feature-scoping intent and the 'true SDD enforcement' goal. The spec must define a file-ownership/feature-mapping contract or explicitly declare global authorization as an accepted non-goal.

The stated security boundary is incomplete. The Problem Statement claims to close the 'primary agents mutate code directly' bypass, but REQ-004 gates only `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`, and `multi_replace_file_content`; shell/`run_command`, git operations, and other mutation paths remain ungated (`sed -i`, `git apply`, script execution). No threat model enumerates which mutation vectors are in or out of scope, and the spec has no non-goals section, so an implementer cannot judge whether this is a deliberate boundary or an oversight. The spec must state the enforcement boundary and either gate or explicitly exclude shell execution.

REQ-001 cannot distinguish a requirement *declaration* from a *citation*. It extracts every regex occurrence in `spec.md`, not declarations. This spec's own `spec.md` contains the literal placeholder `REQ-xxx` (lines 22-23, 35), which the pattern matches and treats as a declared requirement ID; `design.md` and `tasks.md` happen to contain that literal, but `verification.md` does not, so `--verify-evidence` (Task 6 in `tasks.md`) fails on the spec's own package. Conversely, any prose citation of a historical ID becomes a new requirement, and a literal `REQ-xxx` string in `decisions.md` satisfies REQ-001's citation check. The spec must define declaration syntax (e.g., heading/table-anchored) and exclude placeholder tokens.

REQ-001 weakens the traceability contract it claims to enforce. It requires `decisions.md` to contain only *one* `ADR-\d+` or `REQ` citation, and `verification.md` citations only when `--verify-evidence` is set, whereas `rules/spec-standard.md:33` requires every requirement ID to be cited in `decisions.md`, `design.md`, `tasks.md` *and* `verification.md`. REQ-007 asserts rule/skill alignment but never amends this weaker contract, so the implementation will diverge from the authoritative rule the plugin ships. Either REQ-001 or the rule must be changed so one contract is authoritative.

REQ-001 AC3's 'or status `completed` / `implemented`' trigger is unreachable and contradictory. REQ-002 AC1 places `completed` and `implemented` in neither `EXECUTION_STATUSES` nor `PLANNING_STATUSES`, and `validate_spec_package()` is specified to receive only a directory, not a status. In `verify_active_specification` such records are dropped during partitioning and never validated, so the status-triggered evidence check can never fire; conversely a repository whose only spec is `implemented` returns `no_active_spec` and blocks all post-implementation maintenance. The trigger and terminal-status behavior must be defined explicitly.

The observable CLI contract is undefined. REQ-002/REQ-006 add `--feature`, `--allow-planning`, and `--verify-evidence`, but the spec never defines exit codes (current code returns 0/1/2), the `--json` object schema, the shape of the `warnings` list required by REQ-006 AC1, or the precedence when `--feature` selects a planning-stage spec with the default `require_approved=True`. REQ-008 AC2 requires tests for these behaviors, which cannot be written against an unspecified contract; downstream hooks and CI also depend on it.

Hook matcher semantics are undefined and the proposed matcher appears not to satisfy REQ-004 AC1. AC1 requires registration for the four tools 'including `client:` and `default_api:` tool name prefixes', but neither the spec nor design defines whether the matcher is exact, substring, or regex. design.md:122 proposes `"invoke_subagent|write_to_file|replace_file_content|multi_replace_file_content"`, which does not match `client:write_to_file` or `default_api:write_to_file` under exact/fullmatch semantics. The authoritative hook matcher schema must be stated and the matcher shown to cover prefixed names.

The target-path extraction contract is unspecified. REQ-004 AC2 requires resolving a target file path and failing closed when it cannot be resolved, but the spec never names the authoritative argument key per tool (design.md:142 guesses `TargetFile`/`target_file`/`file_path`/`path`) or the base directory for relative paths. `Path(raw).resolve()` resolves against the hook process CWD, which need not equal `workspace_root`, so a legitimate relative write can be misclassified as external (silently allowed by AC2a) or denied. Both outcomes are security- or usability-relevant and are currently left to the implementer.

The workspace root used for every containment and approval decision is not an authoritative value. design.md:105 derives it from `payload.get("cwd")`, `AGY_ACTIVE_WORKSPACE`, or process CWD - all supplied by or influenceable by the same agent the gate is policing. An agent can point the gate at a different repository containing an approved spec and then mutate the real workspace. The spec must name a trusted root source (e.g., runtime-provided project root) and define behavior on mismatch or when the value is absent.

Path containment is incomplete. REQ-003 AC3 applies `Path.is_relative_to(root)` only to `spec_path` candidates, while the first candidate `specs_dir / feature_id` is built from the untrusted Feature ID table cell; the statement says 'all resolved specification paths' but the AC does not require containment for the feat_id-derived candidate, allowing `../..` traversal via INDEX.md. Separately, `resolve()` follows symlinks, so an in-workspace symlink pointing outside the workspace is classified as external and allowed unconditionally by REQ-004 AC2a, bypassing the gate entirely. The spec must require containment checks on every candidate and define symlink handling.

Lifecycle status vocabulary is inconsistent and has no normalization rule. `skills/spec-standard/SKILL.md:96` defines `draft`, `review`, `approved`, `implemented`; the spec adds `planning`, `in-progress`, `active`, `completed`, and `done`. Matching is described as lowercasing only, so a human writing `In Progress` (space) or `Approved ` fails the set test and silently denies execution, while `implemented` is a dead end. REQ-007 requires rule/skill alignment but never reconciles the vocabulary or specifies normalization for case, whitespace, and hyphen/space variants. The canonical status enum and normalization function must be part of the contract.

Several normative requirements are premature internal implementation details masquerading as contracts. REQ-002 AC1 mandates constant names and literal set values; REQ-001 AC2, REQ-003 AC3, and REQ-004 AC2 name private functions (`validate_spec_package`, `verify_active_specification`, `evaluate_spec_gate`); REQ-003 AC3 mandates the `Path.is_relative_to` API (Python 3.9+, with no runtime version declared); REQ-003 AC4 mandates the exact `re.split` lookbehind expression; REQ-005 AC1 mandates regex word-boundary matching and specific keyword-set membership. These lock refactoring and cannot be tested as behavior, while the genuinely observable behaviors (CLI output, exit codes, hook decision payloads, reason strings) are left unspecified. The spec must express behavior/invariants and move these to design.md.

REQ-004 AC2a rests on an unverified assumption about host layout. It asserts that agent runtime artifacts under `<appDataDir>/brain/` resolve outside `workspace_root` and therefore need unconditional allowance. If `appDataDir` is inside the workspace or is cwd-relative, neither AC2a nor AC2b applies, the write is gated, and the Phase 1 planning deadlock the requirement exists to prevent still occurs - while AC2c simultaneously denies unresolvable paths. The spec must state a verified path contract for brain artifacts, or make the exemption an explicit, configurable path list rather than conditional on an unproven resolution outcome.

The gate contradicts the documented fast path and does not define which files it covers. REQ-003 AC1 and REQ-004 AC3 require a complete four-document package for every write outside `docs/specs/` in any repository containing `docs/specs/`, with no exemption, whereas `rules/spec-standard.md:12-13` (which REQ-007 says must be aligned) explicitly exempts single-file typo fixes, one-line bug fixes with regression tests, and minor config changes touching at most one file. REQ-007 never amends the rule's scope, so the documented workflow and the enforced workflow contradict each other. AC3's phrase 'code or configuration file' is also undefined and unimplemented by the described mechanism, which gates every path outside `docs/specs/` including README and documentation.

Acceptance criteria are numbered only locally (1, 2, 3) with no stable `AC-xxx` identifiers, so `tasks.md`, tests, and `verification.md` cannot cite a specific criterion. `rules/spec-standard.md` requires testable acceptance criteria; without stable IDs, REQ-008 AC2's claim of REQ-001..REQ-007 coverage cannot be audited criterion-by-criterion.

REQ-008 AC3 requires pytest to pass 'with 0 failures and 0 external filesystem dependencies' but defines neither how an external filesystem dependency is measured, nor the Python version, nor the exact invocation. REQ-008 AC1's 'zero references ... anywhere in `tests/` or `scripts/`' also matches generated `__pycache__` artifacts present in the repo, making the check ambiguous.

The spec has no Out of Scope / Non-Goals section, no assumptions section, and no rollback or risk section. Section 1 is a problem statement only. Readers cannot determine whether shell execution, git operations, non-SDD repositories, status promotion, or `plugin.json` versioning are in scope, and each of those gaps is consequential for implementation and review.

REQ-005 AC3 enumerates removal of `TRANSLATION_TYPES`, `runs/` checks, and `AGY_ATTENTION_GUARD_OBSERVATION_MODE`, but `scripts/spec-gate.py:17` also defines an unused `EXEMPT_TYPES` constant, and REQ-008 AC1 only greps for `ai-review-plugin`/`TRANSLATION_TYPES`. 'Remove dead code' is not testable without naming the dead symbols, so leftover dead constants can remain while AC3 passes.

REQ-003 AC4 specifies escaped-pipe splitting but not malformed-row handling. `parse_specs_index` currently drops any row with fewer than six cells, so a mistyped or truncated INDEX row (including a draft spec) disappears silently and the gate either reports `no_active_spec` or validates the wrong set. The spec should define strict parsing with diagnostics for malformed rows rather than silent skipping.

REQ-006 AC1's non-blocking guarantee is stated for execution-authorized specs, and design.md step 8 applies the `valid_features`/`warnings` aggregation only when `require_approved` is True. Under `--allow-planning` (`require_approved=False`) a single incomplete draft still aborts validation, so the cross-stream blocking the feature claims to remove persists in exactly the Phase 1 authoring mode the flag exists for. Multi-spec semantics for the planning path must be specified.

Human approval has no auditable record. `Status: Approved` in `spec.md` and INDEX.md is the only evidence; there is no approver identity, timestamp, or approved-scope record, and the spec's version 1.0.0 duplicates `plugin.json`'s 1.0.0 despite a breaking behavior change (mutations previously allowed are now denied). Approval provenance and version-bump policy are unspecified.
